Stop rendering when a claim in your text stops holding

Source: R/text.R
cr_expect.Rd

Put cr_expect() calls in a hidden chunk next to hand-written claims (in the abstract or discussion, say). If a re-run changes the sign or the significance of a result, rendering fails with a message naming the claim, instead of the old sentence silently surviving.

Usage

cr_expect(
  x,
  dv = NULL,
  variable = NULL,
  level = NULL,
  sign = NULL,
  sig = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  action = c("error", "warning"),
  claim = NULL,
  subgroup = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A clean_results/cr_tests object, or a cr_hypotheses object (then every test with an expect is checked).

dv

Outcome name (raw or displayed label).

variable

Predictor or grouping variable, or a coefficient name such as "age". For correlations, the other variable.

level

Factor level as in the data ("LossFraming") or as displayed ("Loss framing"); for contrasts, "Loss vs. Gain" in either form.

sign

"+", "-", or NULL (don't check).

sig

TRUE (must be significant), FALSE (must not be), or NULL.

alpha

Significance threshold.

action

"error" (stop rendering) or "warning".

claim

Optional text of the claim, shown in the message.

subgroup

For tests run with by, which subgroup.

Value

TRUE invisibly when every check passes.
